ns2:section.sectionText: THE POLITICS OF INTERNATIONAL CONSERVATION AND DEVELOPMENT: The problem of how to conserve the earth?s rich biological heritage while enhancing the well-being of some of the world?s poorest people stands as a critical global challenge. This course will examine this complex issue using the lens of political science and related cross-cutting fields such as political ecology and common property. It will demonstrate how insights and approaches from these areas of scholarship can help understand and address the twin problems of biodiversity loss and human poverty in the countries of Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Examples will be drawn from these three geographic areas focusing on forest and wildlife conservation and management.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.
